messages.author: 8e72bac5f7bfb16e
messages.subject: initialization mystery
parts:
In the past, I have had the impression that to start a new shiny session, 'from scratch', it suffices to reload the url pointing to the directory with server.R and ui.R.  So a typical debugging cycle would be to modify server.R and ui.R, reload to test, etc.

Now I reload, and tables contain old values from previous sessions.  What could be happening?

In my server.R, I have initialization code above the call to shinyServer(), which initializes data that should be getting displayed in various renderTable() calls, etc.

If I kill the server process and restart it, then load my shiny url, I get a clean start with properly initialzed values.

Am I right to expect a clean restart on reloading my shiny url?
If yes, any suggestions about what is screwing this up?
If no, is there some other way to get a clean restart besides restarting the server process?

Thanks in advance!

PS. versions are:

> packageVersion('shiny')
[1] ‘0.10.1’
> 

$ shiny-server --version
Shiny Server v1.  2.  1.0
Node.js v0.10.21

messages.author: 3da48b33a2f506a9
messages.subject: Re: initialization mystery
parts:
Norman,

If you initialize your data outside of call to shinyServer(), then what you are seeing is expected. Please refer to this article for more info on scoping:

You can use a restart.txt file that will force a new process to start. Please refer to this section of Admin Guide.


Hope this helps,
Fereshteh

The section you refer to in the admin guide, however, gives the impression that changes to server.R and ui.R will cause

"

Maybe I'll create an initialization function that is called inside of shinyServer().  Somewhat cumbersome, but that should do the trick.
